newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND LOSE ATHERTON AS RAIN INTERVENES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND LOSE ATHERTON AS RAIN INTERVENES.

text.p: England lost captain Mike Atherton cheaply after finally dismissing Zimbabwe for 376 on the second afternoon of the first test at Queen's Club.

From 372 for seven the home side lost three wickets for the addition of just four runs, but struck back through the leg spin of Paul Strang who trapped Atherton lbw for 16 in the last over before tea as England reached 48 for one.
With heavy rain arriving during the tea interval, England were left to reflect on another mixed day with the ball after Zimbabwe had resumed on 256 for six.
They picked up only one wicket before lunch and needed a touch of good fortune to make the breakthrough which hustled the innings to its end.
Heath Streak played a secure backward defensive stroke against left arm seamer Alan Mullally, but the ball ran off the bottom of his bat, through his legs and on to the stumps.

Streak had made 19 of a stand worth 41 with Andy Flower who reached his third test century after toiling for 57 balls in the nervous 90's. But after making 112 from 313 balls with 10 fours, Flower misjudged a reverse sweep against Tufnell and was caught by the diving Stewart.
Henry Olonga then hit his fourth ball straight to Nick Knight at silly point to give Tufnell his second wicket in the over and bring the innings to a close.
